title: Cadet Training
description: Learn the basics on Mars. Watch LIFE, SHIELD, POWER, and FOOD — every choice costs something.
siteNote: Real Mars landing region explored by Perseverance. Good practice ground for junior controllers.
coachTip: Start here! Build a small base, then walk your cadet and face a flare and a dust storm.

title: Lunar Dust Watch
description: Moon outpost: dust can bury solar panels. Decide fast — Earth radio is almost instant, but power still runs out.
siteNote: Artemis target region — long shadows, precious sunlight, and clingy lunar dust.
coachTip: On the Moon, dust and sunlight are the big trade-offs. Retract panels or keep charging?

title: Short Scout
description: Quick Mars scout. Survey the site, keep life support up, and respect the ~20 minute radio delay.
siteNote: Ancient clay-rich plains — a candidate site studied for Mars exploration.

title: Artemis Scout
description: Short lunar stay. Balance power, shielding, and food while Earth is only a second away by radio.
siteNote: Near the lunar south pole — sunlight and cold traps in the same neighborhood.

title: Standard Outpost
description: Full Mars outpost. Balance food, power, shielding, and life support while Earth waits 20 minutes away.
siteNote: River-delta geology; a real NASA mission site you can explore in Mars Trek.

title: Long Stay
description: Extended Mars surface stay. Dust storms, flares, and delayed Earth advice will test your trade-offs.
siteNote: Curiosity's home — real surface conditions and radiation lessons from MSL RAD.
